title: Le Travenues Technology Ltd - 544192 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: ixigo Q1 FY27: record GTV of Rs 5,524 crore (+19% YoY) and PAT of Rs 34.24 crore (+81%), while adjusted EBITDA fell 7% to Rs 29.24 crore as hotels and AI were funded.
summary.overview: Management described the quarter as one where the core businesses (buses, trains, flights) kept growing and gaining share despite the Iran conflict's effect on oil and airfares and train policy constraints on OTAs. Revenue from operations rose 13% to Rs 356.75 crore and contribution margin rose 13% to Rs 144.94 crore at 40.6%. Management said it chose to reinvest part of the core operating leverage into hotels (Brevistay 54.66% acquisition) and AI (ixigo NEXT, TARA, busGDS.ai), which lowered adjusted EBITDA and the 'Others' contribution margin to negative Rs 3.06 crore. Flights volume growth was muted as capacity cuts by Air India and IndiGo weakened the new-to-flying funnel, and management declined to guide on near-term flight growth.

segments.name: Trains
segments.commentary: Segments 2.44 crore (-8% YoY); GTV Rs 2,138.86 crore (+4%); revenue Rs 141.04 crore (+9%); contribution margin Rs 52.74 crore (+29%), margin 37% vs 32%. OTA train market share rose to about 63% from about 60% a few quarters ago; contributed 36% of group contribution margin.

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: Segments 0.29 crore (+4%); GTV Rs 2,341.84 crore (+27%); revenue Rs 104.56 crore; contribution margin Rs 41.04 crore at 39% vs 42% last year. Domestic ATV +22% YoY and international ATV +38% YoY; contributed 28% of group contribution margin.

segments.name: Buses (AbhiBus)
segments.commentary: Passenger segments 0.89 crore (+33%); GTV Rs 947.43 crore (+39%); revenue Rs 102.55 crore (+34%); contribution margin Rs 54.22 crore (+28%) at 53%. Now the largest contributor at 37% of group contribution margin. Management cited GDP growth of 39% YoY.

segments.name: Others (hotels, Zoop and other businesses)
segments.commentary: Contribution margin negative Rs 3.06 crore vs positive Rs 1.86 crore last year, reflecting hotel build-out spend. Management said hotel investment is showing up above the contribution margin line, deliberately.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance on brand marketing spend; management said customer inducement cost (brand performance plus discounts) is targeted at around 4% of GTV where possible, with some quarters above that.
Management expects hotels to have a longer gestation period; the ambition is to become the number one discovery and booking platform for mid-market and budget hotels within four to five years.
Management expects technology cost growth rate to moderate as initial AI platform investment matures, with the long-term aim of technology cost falling as a percentage of revenue year on year.
Management expects flight capacity to recover only around the festive period in Q3, so it remains cautious on near-term aviation passenger growth.
Management said other income (around Rs 29 crore) should not rise substantially.
Management declined to guide on Q2 FY27 flight growth or on margin trajectory, saying growth depends on ATV and supply.
capex_capacity: Brevistay: 54.66% stake acquisition to add direct hotel relationships and flexible-stay inventory; management expects double-digit gross take rates from the combined platform.

Hotels: more than 10,000 directly partnered hotels across nearly 700 towns; several thousand onboarded every quarter; about 0.5 million room-nights (heads on beds) in Q1; HELLO extranet supports conventional and flexible stays.
Budget-hotel Peace of Mind products and a PMS to be tested on select properties, with rollout over the subsequent quarters of FY27.
Capitalisation of AI/platform costs stated to be in the same range as the prior quarter, per the CFO; no absolute number given.
Metro bookings live in five cities; busGDS.ai launched at Prawaas 5.0 for bus operators (setup in as little as 30 minutes).
demand_pricing: Domestic ATV on the platform +22% YoY and +13% QoQ; international ATV +38% YoY and nearly +30% QoQ. DGCA industry passenger growth was about 2% YoY per management.
Air India capacity cut about 20% and IndiGo about 10% for the July-September quarter, per management, with overall domestic capacity shrinking.
Bus net take rate fell QoQ to 10.8%; management said discounting was range-bound over the last 6-8 quarters, and gross take rate is 11-11.5%.
Bus category described as a near-duopoly; management said the company was more disciplined on discounts and marketing this quarter than peers.

Train volumes pressured by Tatkal access changes for OTAs, lower waitlist inventory and extra authentication; management is hopeful about OTP-based authentication for OTAs but is not planning on relief.
AI customer-query resolution by chatbot rose to 92% from 88%; app downloads 3.27 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~80% sequential jump in advertising spend one-time or ongoing, and where should margins go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said Q1 brand spend is seasonal (IPL activity, AbhiBus push) and no brand marketing guidance is given; customer inducement (brand plus discounts) is targeted around 4% of GTV where possible. Saurabh said Q1 spend followed a similar pattern last year and higher take-rate businesses should lift EBITDA over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did flight GTV grow 27% when volume grew only 4%, and will Q2 flight volumes decline sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke attributed the gap to fares: domestic ATV +22% YoY and international +38%, with DGCA industry passenger growth about 2%. He said Air India capacity was cut about 20% and IndiGo about 10% for the July-September quarter and gave no forward call on Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 0.5 million hotel room-nights comes from the existing user base, and how much investment sits in hotels and AI below contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said about 90% of hotel bookings come from already-registered users, and that the 'Others' line moved by roughly Rs 5 crore YoY. Management did not split hotel and AI investment, and Saurabh declined to give a margin guardrail or a multi-year EBITDA path.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise while technology costs were flat QoQ, and what is the AI capitalisation figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh said hotel costs sit across technology and employee lines, and that capitalisation is in the same range as last quarter, with no absolute number given.

qa_highlights.question: Are train contribution margin gains from the Spanish or consolidated business, or organic?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh said train is a small part of the business and that the margin should not be projected forward; costs were cut during the quarter, and the 'Train is Part' initiative is early, with a clearer read in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the easier base support flight growth acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh said growth is a function of ATV and supply, and he cannot forecast macro conditions; he would expect improvement only if the geopolitical situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: Bus net take rate fell QoQ to 10.8%: is discounting rising and will it recover to 11-11.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said 11-11.5% is the gross take rate and that discounting has been range-bound over the last 6-8 quarters, with no intention to get aggressive. The Q1 dip reflected the seasonal AMJ peak with more marketing and discounts, and the company was more disciplined than peers.

risks_watch: Flight growth depends on fares and supply: Air India (about -20%) and IndiGo (about -10%) capacity cuts for July-September, with management expecting recovery only around Q3 festive period.
Adjusted EBITDA fell 7% YoY as hotel and AI spend rises; management gave no margin trajectory or investment ceiling, and Q2 is the next checkpoint.
Train volumes are under pressure from Tatkal, waitlist and authentication changes; management is not planning for OTP-based relief.
Bus net take rate fell to 10.8% QoQ; watch whether discounting stays within the 6-8 quarter range.
Hotel economics are not disclosed (ticket size, take rate, room-night revenue); Brevistay integration and Peace of Mind rollout timing are open items.
Other income (around Rs 29 crore) is expected to stay flat; management also gave no AI capitalisation figure beyond 'same range as last quarter'.
key_quotes: We do not run each quarter to maximize the reported margin of that quarter.
We are choosing to reinvest a part of that into two areas where we see significant long-term opportunity: hotels and AI.
We have never bought market share to win.
Over the next four to five years, our ambition is to become the number one discovery and booking platform for India's mid-market and budget hotels.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the bus, hotel and AI strategy, but openly cautious on near-term aviation and train volumes. Management repeatedly declined to give quantitative guidance on margins, Q2 flight growth, hotel economics and AI capitalisation, citing macro uncertainty and competitive sensitivity.

adds.what: Brevistay 54.66% stake acquisition adding direct hotel relationships and flexible-stay inventory (not a capacity build-out)
Budget-hotel Peace of Mind products and PMS to be tested on select properties, rollout over subsequent quarters of FY27

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management declined to guide on Q2 flight growth or margins, expects flight capacity to recover only around Q3 festive period, and backs near-term growth with share gains (trains OTA share ~63%, bus GDP +39%) rather than new capacity.
